steps.title: NVIDIA's release goes in, a flash package comes out
steps.body:
The build runs top to bottom in five stages: fetch, rootfs, kernel, image and flash. Everything lands in one NVIDIA-style directory tree.

No SD-card image is assembled. The result is a `Linux_for_Tegra/` tree plus the signed images that NVIDIA's tool generates from it.

steps.title: Two downloads are always needed
steps.body:
`./build.sh fetch` downloads every file and verifies it against a pinned sha256. The driver package (715 MB, `Jetson_Linux_r36.4.3_aarch64.tbz2`) holds the flash tools, firmware binaries and a stock kernel.

The sample root filesystem (1.8 GB) is an Ubuntu 22.04 (jammy) arm64 userland. Without either one there is nothing to flash.

steps.title: Two more downloads, only for your own kernel
steps.body:
The dashed cards are optional. Public sources (226 MB) hold the kernel, NVIDIA modules and device trees. The reference toolchain (140 MB) is GCC 11.3 and runs on x86-64 only.

If you are happy with the stock kernel from the driver package, you can skip both.

steps.title: rootfs builds the operating system tree
steps.body:
It unpacks the sample rootfs with `sudo tar xpf`, keeping owners and permissions. `apply_binaries.sh` adds NVIDIA libraries, stock kernel modules, `extlinux.conf` and the initrd.

`l4t_create_default_user.sh` creates the login account, so there is no first-boot wizard. These steps need root so that file ownership stays correct.

steps.title: kernel compiles your own kernel, modules and device trees
steps.body:
It extracts the sources, applies `patches/source/*.patch`, runs `make defconfig` plus `config/kernel/*.cfg`, and builds `Image`, `dtbs` and modules. NVIDIA's out-of-tree modules are built separately.

It installs the results into `rootfs/lib/modules`, `kernel/Image` and `kernel/dtb/`, and rebuilds the initrd. This stage is optional.

steps.title: image runs NVIDIA's tool in no-flash mode
steps.body:
`sudo l4t_initrd_flash.sh --no-flash` is given the QSPI layout (`flash_t234_qspi.xml`), the external-device layout (`flash_l4t_t234_nvme.xml`) and the board `jetson-orin-nano-devkit-super`. The root device may be nvme0n1p1, SD or USB.

It builds the signed QSPI images, the APP rootfs image and the flashing initrd, and stops without touching a board.

steps.title: Linux_for_Tegra is the real build artifact
steps.body:
NVIDIA's scripts only work from inside their own directory layout, so this tree is the product of the build.

It contains `rootfs/`, `kernel/Image` (flashed to the `kernel` partition), `kernel/dtb/` (device trees and UEFI overlays), `bootloader/` (the MB1, MB2, UEFI and other binaries), the board `.conf` with `flash.sh`, and `tools/kernel_flash/` with the generated images.

steps.title: flash writes the package to the board in recovery mode
steps.body:
`sudo l4t_initrd_flash.sh --flash-only --network usb0` boots a recovery initrd over USB and then writes everything. It needs the board in recovery mode.

The flash-flow diagram shows these steps one by one.

steps.title: Firmware goes to the module, the OS to your drive
steps.body:
QSPI-NOR (64 MiB on the module) gets the boot firmware in two copies, A_ and B_. The SD card, NVMe or USB drive gets `kernel`, `kernel-dtb`, the ESP and `APP`, the root filesystem.

So the same package writes two different devices.

steps.anchor: Steps run as your user except where sudo is shown
steps.title: Read it first with --dry-run
steps.body:
Steps run as your user except where `sudo` is shown, because root-owned files must be created as root.

Everything is explained command by command in `./build.sh --dry-run all`, which prints every command with its reason and runs nothing.
